HOAX: This UNAIDS job advert in Uganda is fake

A UNAIDS Communications officer told PesaCheck that the job advertisement is fake.

A Facebook post advertising job opportunities at the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and AIDS (UNAIDS) in Uganda is a HOAX.

The poster has a UNAIDS logo and lists several openings available in 2022.

The opportunities include internships, clerical officers, office secretaries, data entry clerks and drivers. Others are office administrators, technical support staff, field officers, junior accountants and trainers of trainees.

The advert claims that the UN agency is recruiting for the above vacancies in all districts of Uganda. Interested applicants should send scanned copies of their curriculum vitae and cover letters to an Outlook email account.

The advert promises to contact applicants immediately after the application deadline. The poster has also been shared here.

However, the email listed in the advert is fake. A look at the contact details of UNAIDS on its website shows that the end of their official emails is from the website domain, unaids.org.

In addition, the listed opportunities are non-existent on the official website of UNAIDS.

Pere Mora Romà, a UNAIDS Global Communications team member told PesaCheck in an email that the advert was fake.

“Thank you for reporting this. This is totally fake.”

PesaCheck has looked into a Facebook post advertising job opportunities at the United Nations Programme on HIV/AIDS (UNAIDS) and finds it to be a HOAX.

This post is part of an ongoing series of PesaCheck fact-checks examining content marked as potential misinformation on Facebook and other social media platforms.

By partnering with Facebook and similar social media platforms, third-party fact-checking organisations like PesaCheck are helping to sort fact from fiction. We do this by giving the public deeper insight and context to posts they see in their social media feeds.

PesaCheck is East Africa’s first public finance fact-checking initiative. It was co-founded by Catherine Gicheru and Justin Arenstein, and is being incubated by the continent’s largest civic technology and data journalism accelerator: Code for Africa. It seeks to help the public separate fact from fiction in public pronouncements about the numbers that shape our world, with a special emphasis on pronouncements about public finances that shape government’s delivery of Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) public services, such as healthcare, rural development and access to water / sanitation. PesaCheck also tests the accuracy of media reportage. To find out more about the project, visit pesacheck.org.

PesaCheck is an initiative of Code for Africa, through its innovateAFRICA fund, with support from Deutsche Welle Akademie, in partnership with a coalition of local African media and other civic watchdog organisations.
